sentences.text: The name Prognathodon translates to "forejaw tooth" from Latin and Greek roots.
This marine reptile is characterized by its massively built jaws and teeth.
A 1.8-meter-long juvenile fossil preserves the outline of a bilobed tail fluke resembling a shark's tail.
The Prognathodon saturator specimen from Maastricht is approximately 12 meters long and is displayed at the Natural History Museum at Maastricht.
The genus Prognathodon was described by Louis Dollo in 1889 based on specimens collected in Belgium.
An intact fossil skull was discovered in 1998 in the Maastricht limestone quarries.
In 2009, P. hudae was described by Hani F. Kaddumi from fossils found in the Muwaqqar Chalk Marl Formation of Harrana, Jordan.
P. primus was described in 2009 based on an articulated upper skull, representing the first near-complete mosasaur skull found in the Middle East.
In some species, teeth extended forward like Triassic placodonts, suggesting a diet of shellfish, large fish, and sea turtles.
Prognathodon is generally considered a generalist predator.
Stomach contents in a Canadian fossil included a sea turtle, large fish like barracuda and trout, and a possible cephalopod.
Studies of preserved teeth and gut contents have helped infer the paleoecology of Prognathodon.
The type species of the genus is Prognathodon solvayi.
Prognathodon belongs to the Mosasaurinae subfamily, which also includes Mosasaurus and Clidastes.
Former names for Prognathodon include Prognathosaurus, Dollosaurus, Brachysaurana, Ancylocentrum, Tenerasaurus, Tylosaurus capensis, and Taniwhasaurus capensis.
Prognathodon lived during the Late Cretaceous.
Fossils of Prognathodon date from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages.
Prognathodon fossils have been found in the Middle East, Europe, New Zealand, Africa, and North America from the Campanian to Maastrichtian ages.
Prognathodon fossils have been found in what is now North America, Europe, and Africa.
The systematics of Prognathodon and the validity of its species are controversial due to specimen differences and incompleteness.
It is debated whether certain species should be assigned to genera like Dollosaurus and Brachysaurana rather than Prognathodon.
A 2022 study suggested T. capensis is a chimera of Prognathodon and Taniwhasaurus, though it remains unidentifiable at the species level.
Some researchers classify P. lutugini in its own genus, Dollosaurus, while others place it within Prognathodon.
